pr_title: Add an option to use malloc for page cache instead of mmap
pr_body:
Fixes #13133

##### Summary
Add a config option `page cache uses malloc` to switch from using mmap to malloc. In some cases mmap will fail whereas malloc works just fine. 

In in the netdata.conf `[global]` section

add the following so that the agent will use malloc instead of mmap (the default is `no`) 

`page cache uses malloc = yes`

##### Test Plan
- Agent should work as this change affects only how the metric page is allocated / deallocated

issue_context.title: [Bug]: Netdata Crash (netdata FATAL : DBENGINE : Cannot allocate dbengine page cache page, with mmap() # : Invalid argument)
issue_context.body:
### Bug description

I experience crashes of the netdata process with the new 1.35.0 / 1.35.1 versions.

From netdata error.log:
`netdata FATAL : DBENGINE : Cannot allocate dbengine page cache page, with mmap() # : Invalid argument`

I run a master server with 6 clients streaming to it (Server: 8 Cores, 48GB RAM). 
The master stores everything within a large dbengine: 
  ```
  memory mode = dbengine
  page cache size = 20000
  dbengine multihost disk space = 96000
  ```
 
This holds a lot of data (apx. 70 days history every 1 second, for master + all clients).
The page cache size is set to this large value intentionally since the physical hard disks are very slow and caching is needed.

When I now pick one of the servers in dashboard and zoom out to max, netdata allocates a lot of memory (up to about 20 GB) which is as intended. But when I continue to look at different charts then the "mmap()" error occurs. It seems the 20GB is a magical limit (might be related with the page cache size).

However the netdata 1.34.1 release version can allocate 32GB RAM easily and whatever "stress" I put to it (zoom out, look at different charts, ...) it never crashes.

I observed a similar behavior and crashes with 1.34.x snapshot builds (before 1.35.0 release) and found the new memory allocator was responsible for it. Then I saw the commit that the mmap was replaced with malloc and thought 1.35.0 release would be good to use... But there seem to be still some mmap problems inside.



### Expected behavior

no crash (like in 1.34.1 and before)

### Steps to reproduce

1. large dataset in dbengine (96 GB), system with RAM 48 GB, large pagecache
2. use dashboard zoom out to max and look at multiple charts => netdata allocates more and more ram
3. when netdata allocated 20GB RAM then the crash happens every time a new chart is looked at (and more date should be loaded).

comments: @stohn thank you for reporting this. In our tests we have used a page cache size of 30000 without problems (collecting 90K+ metrics per second), but looks like something is not quite right (in general).  We will add an option to switch to malloc.

review_comments: FWIW, I think netdata_mmap sets the MAP_ANONYMOUS flag which will cause the pages to be 0-initialized.
The page allocation with malloc used to be exactly like that
